questions.question: How many chambers are there in the heart of amphibians?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amphibians possess a **three-chambered heart**, which is a significant evolutionary step from the two-chambered hearts seen in fish.
 
• The heart structure consists of **two atria** (the right atrium and the left atrium) and **one single ventricle**.
 
• The **right atrium** receives **deoxygenated blood** from the various body organs, while the **left atrium** receives **oxygenated blood** from the **lungs** and the **skin** (which also acts as a respiratory organ).
 
• Both atria pump blood into the single **ventricle**, where some degree of **mixing** of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood occurs before it is pumped out to the rest of the body and the respiratory surfaces.
 
• This arrangement facilitates **double circulation**, although it is considered **incomplete** because the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams are not fully separated in the ventricle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fish (Pisces)**:

 
 
• Fish have a **two-chambered heart** consisting of **one atrium** and **one ventricle**.
 
• They exhibit **single circulation**, where the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the **gills**, and from there, it goes directly to the rest of the body.
 
 
 
• **Reptiles**:
 
 
• Most reptiles have a **three-chambered heart** with a **partially divided ventricle**, which reduces the mixing of blood.
 
• However, **crocodiles**, **alligators**, and **gavials** are unique among reptiles as they possess a fully functional **four-chambered heart**.
 
 
 
• **Birds and Mammals**:
 
 
• These groups possess a **four-chambered heart** with **two atria** and **two ventricles**.
 
• This structure ensures the **complete separation** of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, allowing for high **metabolic efficiency** required for **warm-blooded** (endothermic) animals.
 
 
 
• **Amphibian Respiration**:
 
 
• Because the **three-chambered heart** allows for some blood mixing, amphibians (such as **frogs**, **toads**, and **salamanders**) often supplement their oxygen intake through **cutaneous respiration** (breathing through their **moist skin**).
 
• This is particularly important during periods when they are submerged in water or during **hibernation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **atrium** is the receiving chamber of the heart, while the **ventricle** is the main pumping chamber.
 
• In **Amphibians**, the **3** chambers allow for a more complex circulatory route called the **pulmocutaneous circuit**, which directs blood to the gas-exchange tissues in the lungs and skin.
 
• The evolution of the heart from **2** chambers in fish to **3** in amphibians and finally **4** in mammals reflects the increasing energy demands of animals as they moved from aquatic to terrestrial environments.

questions.question: The term ‘Samyakcharitra’ in Jainism refers to ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right conduct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Jainism, the path to **liberation** (Moksha) is defined by the **Triratna** or the **Three Jewels**. **Samyakcharitra** is the third of these jewels and translates literally to **Right conduct**.
 
• **Samyakcharitra** refers to the practice of living a life based on the principles of Jainism, ensuring that one's actions do not lead to the accumulation of new **Karma** and help in the shedding of old **Karma**.
 
• It involves the strict adherence to ethical and moral codes, specifically the avoidance of harm to all living beings, which is the core tenet of **Ahimsa**.
 
• While **Samyak Darshana** (Right Faith) provides the vision and **Samyak Jnana** (Right Knowledge) provides the understanding, **Samyak Charitra** is the practical application of those beliefs in daily life. ***Hence, the correct answer is Right conduct.***
 
• The practice of **Right conduct** is divided into two categories: **Mahavratas** (five great vows) for Jain monks and **Anuvratas** (five small vows) for laypersons or householders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Triratna (The Three Jewels):**

 
 
• **Samyak Darshana (Right Faith/Perception):** This refers to having the correct **vision** or belief in the true nature of reality. It is the starting point of the spiritual journey in Jainism, involving the belief in the **Tirthankaras** and their teachings.
 
• **Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge):** This is the **accurate and doubt-free knowledge** of the soul (Jiva) and the non-soul (Ajiva). It requires studying the Jain scriptures and understanding the **Anekantavada** (theory of many-sidedness).
 
• **Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct):** As established, this is the ethical **integration** of faith and knowledge into action.
 
 
 
• **The Five Vows of Jainism:**
 
 
• **Ahimsa:** Non-violence toward all living beings.
 
• **Satya:** Truthfulness in speech and thought.
 
• **Asteya:** Non-stealing or not taking what is not given.
 
• **Brahmacharya:** Chastity or sexual continence (added by **Lord Mahavira**, the **24th Tirthankara**).
 
• **Aparigraha:** Non-attachment or non-possession of worldly goods.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** Jainism is an ancient Indian religion. **Lord Rishabhdev** was the **1st Tirthankara**, while **Lord Parshvanatha** was the **23rd**. **Lord Mahavira** (born in **599 BCE**) popularized the **Triratna** and the five-fold path to achieve **Kaivalya** (omniscience).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ultimate goal of following the **Triratna** is to attain **Moksha**, which is the liberation of the soul from the cycle of **birth and death**.
 
• **Right Conduct** is not just about external actions but also internal purity. It includes **Samiti** (carefulness in movement) and **Gupti** (restraint of mind, speech, and body).
 
• In Jain philosophy, **Karma** is viewed as a physical substance that sticks to the soul due to passions (**Kashayas**) like anger, pride, and greed. **Samyakcharitra** serves as the shield that stops the influx of this matter (**Samvara**).
 
• The distinction between **Digambara** and **Svetambara** sects also involves slight variations in the interpretation of conduct, particularly regarding clothing and possessions.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is traditionally performed in the state of Nagaland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leshalaptu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Leshalaptu** is a traditional folk dance originating from the state of **Nagaland** in **Northeast India**.
 
• This dance is specifically performed by **women** and is characterized by its rhythmic and graceful movements that showcase the cultural richness of the **Naga** people.
 
• It is one of the many vibrant dance forms of the state, often performed during social gatherings and **tribal festivals** to celebrate the community's heritage.
 
• The dancers wear traditional **tribal costumes**, which typically include colorful **hand-woven shawls**, ethnic beads, and unique **jewelry** that vary from tribe to tribe.
 
• The performance of **Leshalaptu** highlights the significant role of women in preserving the oral and physical traditions of the **Naga tribes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shon:**

 
 
• **Shon** is a traditional dance from **Ladakh**, often referred to as the **"Royal Dance"** because it was historically performed for the **King (Lama)** of Ladakh.
 
• It is performed on special occasions, and the dancers move in a slow, dignified manner accompanied by the sounds of the **Surna** (oboe) and **Daman** (drum).
 
 
 
• **Phulpati:**
 
 
• This folk dance belongs to the **Malwa region** of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is primarily performed by **unmarried girls** during the **Holi** festival as a celebration of nature and the arrival of spring.
 
 
 
• **Lezim:**
 
 
• **Lezim** is a popular folk dance from the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• The dance is named after a small musical instrument called the **Lezim**, which consists of a wooden stick with jingling **cymbals** attached to a chain.
 
• It is a high-energy dance form frequently seen during the **Ganesh Chaturthi** festival and other cultural processions.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland:**
 
 
• Located in **Northeast India**, **Nagaland** became the **16th state** of the Indian Union on **1st December 1963**.
 
• The state capital is **Kohima**, and the largest city is **Dimapur**.
 
• It is home to several major tribes, including the **Angami**, **Ao**, **Sumi**, **Konyak**, and **Rengma**, each having its own distinct festivals and dances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hornbill Festival:** Often called the **"Festival of Festivals,"** it is held every year from **1st to 10th December** at **Kisama Heritage Village** to encourage inter-tribal interaction and promote the cultural heritage of **Nagaland**.
 
• **War Dance:** One of the most prominent dance styles in **Nagaland**, usually performed by men involving mock combat movements, **spears**, and **shields**.
 
• **Bailadila:** While not a dance, it's worth noting the **Naga** culture is deeply rooted in **agriculture**, and many dances like the **Zeliang dance** or **Bamboo dance** (similiar to **Cheraw**) are linked to harvest cycles.
 
• **Moatsu Mong:** A major festival of the **Ao tribe** celebrated in **May** after the completion of the sowing season, featuring vigorous singing and dancing.
 
• **Sekrenyi:** A purification festival celebrated by the **Angami tribe** in **February**, marking the start of a new lunar year with traditional rituals.

questions.question: Which of the following organ secretes adrenaline in animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adrenal gland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Adrenal glands** are small, triangular-shaped endocrine glands located on the **superior aspect** (top) of both **kidneys**.
 
• These glands are responsible for secreting **adrenaline** (also known as **epinephrine**) and **noradrenaline** (**norepinephrine**) from the **adrenal medulla**, which is the inner part of the gland.
 
• **Adrenaline** is primarily known as the **"emergency hormone"** or the **"fight-or-flight"** hormone because it is secreted rapidly in response to **stress**, **danger**, or **extreme emotions**.
 
• The primary **function** of adrenaline is to prepare the body for immediate physical action by increasing the **heart rate**, elevating **blood pressure**, and dilating the **bronchioles** in the lungs to increase oxygen intake.
 
• It also stimulates the **breakdown of glycogen** into **glucose** in the liver, increasing **blood sugar levels** to provide a sudden surge of **energy** to the muscles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pituitary Gland**:

 
 
• Often referred to as the **"Master Gland,"** it is located at the **base of the brain**, just below the **hypothalamus**.
 
• It secretes various essential hormones, including **Growth Hormone (GH)**, **Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)**, and **Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)**, which regulate other endocrine glands.
 
 
 
• **Thyroid Gland**:
 
 
• This **butterfly-shaped** gland is located in the **neck**, in front of the **trachea**.
 
• It produces **Thyroxine (T4)** and **Triiodothyronine (T3)**, which play a critical role in regulating the body's **metabolic rate**, **body temperature**, and **growth**.
 
 
 
• **Thymus Gland**:
 
 
• Located in the **upper chest** behind the **sternum**, it is a vital part of the **immune system** during early life.
 
• It secretes **thymosin**, a hormone necessary for the **maturation** and development of **T-lymphocytes** (T-cells).
 
• The gland is most active during **childhood** and begins to **shrink (atrophy)** after **puberty**, being replaced by **fatty tissue** in adults.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Adrenal gland** is divided into two distinct structures: the **Adrenal Cortex** (outer layer) and the **Adrenal Medulla** (inner layer).
 
• The **Adrenal Cortex** produces **corticosteroids** such as **Cortisol** (involved in metabolism and stress response) and **Aldosterone** (which regulates **salt and water balance**).
 
• In **medical applications**, synthetic adrenaline is used in **EpiPens** to treat **anaphylaxis** (severe allergic reactions) by reversing **low blood pressure** and opening **airways**.
 
• The **Endocrine System** utilizes these hormones as **chemical messengers** that travel through the **bloodstream** to reach target **organs** and maintain **homeostasis**.

questions.question: ‘Pushkar fair’ is held in which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pushkar Fair**, also known as the **Pushkar Camel Fair** or locally as **Kartik Mela**, is an annual multi-day livestock fair and cultural fete held in the town of **Pushkar**.
 
• It is held in the **Ajmer** district of the state of **Rajasthan**, **India**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rajasthan.***
 
• The fair is one of the world's largest **camel** and **livestock** fairs, attracting thousands of traders who bring **camels**, **horses**, and **cattle** for sale and purchase.
 
• The event is celebrated during the Hindu lunar month of **Kartika**, typically falling in **October** or **November**.
 
• The fair culminates on **Kartika Purnima** (the full moon day), which is the most auspicious day for pilgrims to take a holy dip in the **Pushkar Lake**.
 
• It has become a significant **tourist attraction**, drawing visitors from across the globe to witness traditional Rajasthani culture, folk music, and dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Religious Significance:**

 
 
• Pushkar is home to the only prominent temple dedicated to **Lord Brahma** in the world, which dates back to the **14th century**.
 
• The **Pushkar Lake** is surrounded by **52 ghats** where devotees perform prayers and religious rituals.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Activities:**
 
 
• The fair features unique competitions such as the **"longest moustache"** contest, "matka phod", and bridal competitions.
 
• **Camel races** and decorated camel parades are the hallmark features of the festivities.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The fair is a vital source of income for local **artisans**, **traders**, and the **hospitality** sector in **Rajasthan**.
 
• It promotes **rural tourism** and showcases the vibrant heritage of the **Thar Desert** region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location and Geography:** **Pushkar** is situated at an average elevation of **510 meters** and is nestled between the **Aravalli Range** hills.
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Bihar:** Famous for the **Sonepur Cattle Fair**, which is another of the largest livestock fairs in **Asia**, held at the confluence of the **Ganges** and **Gandak** rivers.
 
• **Punjab:** Known for festivals like **Baisakhi** and **Hola Mohalla**, which reflect the martial and agricultural spirit of the state.
 
• **Kerala:** Renowned for temple festivals like **Thrissur Pooram** and the **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** held in the backwaters.
 
 
 
• **Recent Trends:** In recent years, the **Rajasthan Tourism Department** has introduced **hot air balloon** flights during the fair to provide a panoramic view of the massive gathering and the desert landscape.

questions.question: In 1600, which English Queen granted a charter to the East India Company, giving it exclusive trading rights with the East?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Queen Elizabeth I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **December 31, 1600**, **Queen Elizabeth I** granted a **Royal Charter** to the **"Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies."**
 
• This charter granted the **East India Company (EIC)** a **monopoly** on English trade with all countries east of the **Cape of Good Hope** and west of the **Straits of Magellan**.
 
• The initial charter provided the company with exclusive trading rights for a period of **15 years**, which was later extended indefinitely by **King James I** in **1609**.
 
• The primary motivation behind the charter was to compete with the **Dutch** and **Portuguese** who were already profiting from the **spice trade** in the **East Indies** (present-day Indonesia and Southeast Asia).
 
• At the time this charter was signed in **1600**, the **Mughal Empire** in India was being ruled by **Emperor Akbar**, who reigned until **1605**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Queen Victoria**:

 
 
• She reigned from **1837 to 1901**, which was much later than the formation of the company.
 
• Following the **Revolt of 1857**, the **Government of India Act 1858** transferred the administration of India from the Company to the **British Crown**.
 
• She was proclaimed the **Empress of India** (Kaiser-i-Hind) in **1876** at the **Delhi Durbar**.
 
 
 
• **Queen Mary I**:
 
 
• Commonly known as **"Bloody Mary,"** she ruled **England** and **Ireland** from **1553 until 1558**.
 
• She was the elder half-sister of **Queen Elizabeth I** and was focused on restoring **Catholicism** in England rather than eastern trade expansion.
 
 
 
• **Queen Anne**:
 
 
• She reigned from **1702 to 1714**.
 
• Her reign is most notable for the **Acts of Union 1707**, which united the kingdoms of **England** and **Scotland** into a single sovereign state called **Great Britain**.
 
 
 
• **The East India Company's Evolution**:
 
 
• The company eventually shifted its focus from **spices** to commodities like **cotton, silk, indigo dye, saltpeter, and tea**.
 
• It transitioned from a purely commercial entity to a **ruling power** in India after the **Battle of Plassey** in **1757** and the **Battle of Buxar** in **1764**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Early Expeditions**: The first voyage of the company took place in **1601** under the command of **James Lancaster**, reaching **Bantam** in the East Indies.
 
• **Entry into India**: The company's first ship, **Hector**, reached **Surat** in **1608**. **Captain William Hawkins** visited the court of the Mughal Emperor **Jahangir** to seek trade concessions but was initially unsuccessful due to Portuguese influence.
 
• **Sir Thomas Roe**: In **1615**, **King James I** sent **Sir Thomas Roe** as an ambassador to the court of **Jahangir**, successfully securing a **royal farman** (decree) to establish factories at **Surat** and other places.
 
• **Charter Act of 1813**: This act was a major turning point as it ended the company's **monopoly** over Indian trade, though it retained the monopoly over trade with **China** and the trade in **tea**.
 
• **Charter Act of 1833**: This act brought an end to the **East India Company's** commercial activities entirely, turning it into a purely **administrative body** for the British possessions in India.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the 'Bushu' festival traditionally celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bushu**, popularly known as **Bushu Dima**, is the most significant post-harvest festival of the **Dimasa Kachari** community.
 
• It is traditionally celebrated in the state of **Nagaland** and parts of **Assam**. In **Nagaland**, the festival is observed with great enthusiasm in regions like **Dimapur** and **Dhansiri**.
 
• The festival is generally celebrated in the month of **January**, specifically on **January 27th** every **year**, after the harvest is safely gathered in the granaries.
 
• Depending on the duration and scale of the celebration, **Bushu** is categorized into three types: **Bushu Jidap** (celebrated for **3 days**), **Surem Bushu** (celebrated for **5 days**), and **Hangseu Bushu** (a grand celebration lasting **7 days** or more).
 
• The celebration involves community feasts, traditional **Dimasa** folk dances like **Baiba**, and the playing of indigenous musical instruments such as the **Muri** (a long wooden flute) and **Kharam** (drum).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Festivals of Nagaland:**

 
 
• **Nagaland** is often called the **'Land of Festivals'**. The most famous is the **Hornbill Festival**, held in the first week of **December** at **Kisama Heritage Village**, which features all **16 major tribes** of the state.
 
• Other tribal festivals include **Sekrenyi** (celebrated by the **Angami** tribe in **February**), **Moatsu** (celebrated by the **Ao** tribe in **May**), and **Aoleang** (celebrated by the **Konyak** tribe in **April**).
 
 
 
• **Festivals in Bihar:**
 
 
• **Chhath Puja** is the most important ancient Hindu festival dedicated to the **Sun God** and **Chhathi Maiya**. It is observed on the **sixth day** of the lunar month of **Kartika**.
 
• Other notable festivals include **Sama Chakeva**, **Bihula**, and the **Sonepur Cattle Fair**, which is one of the largest livestock fairs in **Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Festivals in Punjab:**
 
 
• **Baisakhi** is the major harvest festival celebrated in **April**, marking the **Sikh New Year** and the formation of the **Khalsa Panth** in **1699**.
 
• **Lohri** is celebrated in **January** to mark the end of peak winter and the arrival of longer days, characterized by bonfires and folk songs.
 
 
 
• **Festivals in Karnataka:**
 
 
• **Ugadi** is the **New Year** festival for the people of the **Deccan** region, celebrated with the preparation of 'Bevu Bella'.
 
• **Kambala** is a traditional **buffalo race** held annually in coastal **Karnataka** districts like **Dakshina Kannada** and **Udupi**.

questions.question: Which of the following incidents took place on 13 April 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**, also known as the **Amritsar Massacre**, took place on **13 April 1919**, which coincided with the festival of **Baisakhi**.
 
• A large, peaceful crowd had gathered at the **Jallianwala Bagh** in **Amritsar**, **Punjab**, to protest the arrest of pro-independence activists **Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew** and **Dr. Satyapal**.
 
• **Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer** entered the area, blocked the only narrow exit, and ordered his troops to fire on the unarmed crowd without any warning.
 
• The firing lasted for about **10 minutes**, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of people and leaving thousands injured, according to various records.
 
• In protest against this horrific incident, **Rabindranath Tagore** renounced his **Knighthood**, and **Mahatma Gandhi** returned the **Kaisar-i-Hind** gold medal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha Movement (1917)**:

 
 
• This was the **first Satyagraha movement** led by **Mahatma Gandhi** in **India**, specifically in the **Champaran** district of **Bihar**.
 
• It was organized to protest against the **Tinkathia system**, where peasants were forced by British planters to grow **Indigo** on **3/20th** of their land.
 
 
 
• **Ahmedabad Mill Workers Movement (1918)**:
 
 
• This movement involved a dispute between **cotton mill owners** and **workers** in **Ahmedabad** regarding the discontinuation of the **Plague Bonus**.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** intervened and undertook his **first hunger strike** in **India** to demand a **35%** wage increase for the workers.
 
 
 
• **Chauri-Chaura Incident (1922)**:
 
 
• Occurred on **4 February 1922** (some sources cite 5 February) at **Chauri Chaura** in the **Gorakhpur** district of the **United Provinces** (modern-day **Uttar Pradesh**).
 
• A large group of protesters participating in the **Non-Cooperation Movement** clashed with police, who opened fire. In retaliation, the demonstrators attacked and set fire to a police station, killing **22 policemen**.
 
• This violence led **Mahatma Gandhi** to call off the **Non-Cooperation Movement** on **12 February 1922**.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act (1919)**:
 
 
• Formally known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act**, it was passed in **March 1919** by the **Imperial Legislative Council**.
 
• It authorized the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism for up to **two years** without trial, leading to widespread protests across **India**.

• Years later, in **1940**, **Udham Singh** assassinated **Michael O'Dwyer** in **London** as an act of revenge for the massacre.

questions.question: What is the name of the two spacecrafts involved in the Proba-3 mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coronagraph and Occulter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Proba-3** mission is a pioneering project by the **European Space Agency (ESA)** designed to demonstrate high-precision **formation flying** in space.
 
• The mission consists of two distinct spacecraft: the **Coronagraph** spacecraft (CSC) and the **Occulter** spacecraft (OSC).
 
• The primary objective of these two satellites is to act as a single, giant **solar coronagraph**. The **Occulter** spacecraft flies approximately **150 meters** in front of the **Coronagraph** spacecraft to block the direct light of the **Sun**.
 
• By perfectly aligning the two satellites, the **Occulter** casts a shadow precisely over the **Coronagraph’s** lens, allowing the latter to observe the **Sun’s inner corona**, which is usually invisible due to the Sun's intense glare.
 
• This formation requires extreme precision, maintaining their relative positions within **millimeter-level accuracy** while orbiting the **Earth** in a **Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch Details:** The **Proba-3** mission was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** using the **PSLV-C59** (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) rocket. The launch took place from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** in **Sriharikota** in **December 2024**.
 
• **Scientific Significance:** The mission aims to study the **solar corona** in visible light. Understanding the corona is vital for predicting **Space Weather**, **Solar Winds**, and **Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs)**, which can impact satellite communications and power grids on **Earth**.
 
• **Project for On-Board Autonomy (Proba):** The **Proba** series is part of **ESA’s** technology demonstration program. Previous missions include **Proba-1** (Earth observation), **Proba-2** (solar observation), and **Proba-V** (vegetation monitoring).
 
• **Technical Innovation:** **Proba-3** is the world’s first mission to maintain such a rigid large-scale structure in space using two independent satellites rather than a single physical structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Spacecraft Roles:** The **Occulter** spacecraft weighs approximately **250 kg** and carries the occulting disk, while the **Coronagraph** spacecraft weighs about **300 kg** and carries the scientific camera and instruments.
 
• **Mission Orbit:** The satellites operate in a **19.7-hour orbit**. The formation flying and scientific observations occur during the **6-hour period** near the **apogee** (the point farthest from Earth), where gravity effects are minimized, allowing for stable alignment.
 
• **International Collaboration:** While led by **ESA**, the mission involves a consortium of **European** industries and a significant partnership with **ISRO** for the launch services, highlighting global cooperation in space exploration.

questions.question: As per the 5th report of National Family Health Survey (2019-21) the sex ratio of total population of India (females per 1000 males) is _____.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)** conducted between **2019-21**, the sex ratio for the total population in India is **1020 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This is a landmark finding as it is the first time in any major national survey or census in India that the number of women has exceeded the number of men.
 
• In comparison, the previous **NFHS-4 (2015-16)** recorded a sex ratio of **991 females per 1000 males**, showing a positive upward trend in the female population ratio.
 
• The survey highlights a significant disparity between residential areas: the **rural sex ratio** stands at **1037**, while the **urban sex ratio** is recorded at **985**.
 
• The **Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB)** has also seen an improvement, rising from **919** in **NFHS-4** to **929** in **NFHS-5**, although it still remains below the natural equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nodal Agency:** The **International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS)**, located in **Mumbai**, is the designated nodal agency for the **National Family Health Survey**.
 
• **Funding and Oversight:** The survey is conducted under the aegis of the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**, Government of India, with technical assistance from **ICF International** and funding from **USAID**.
 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR):** The **NFHS-5** reported that India's **TFR** has declined to **2.0**, which is below the **replacement level of fertility (2.1)**.
 
• **Institutional Births:** There has been a substantial increase in **institutional births**, rising from **78.9%** in the previous survey to **88.6%** in **NFHS-5**, indicating better access to healthcare facilities.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** The survey noted that the percentage of **women having a bank or savings account** that they themselves use increased significantly to **78.6%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Census 2011:** It is important to note the difference between survey data and census data. The **Census of 2011** recorded a sex ratio of **943 females per 1000 males**, which was the last comprehensive enumeration of the entire population.
 
• **Policy Impact:** The improvement in the sex ratio is often attributed to the success of government schemes like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** (launched in **2015**) and various **maternal health** initiatives.
 
• **Life Expectancy:** Experts suggest that the higher sex ratio in the total population is partly due to the fact that **women generally have a higher life expectancy** than men, leading to a larger surviving female population in older age groups.
 
• **Survey Scope:** **NFHS-5** provided data for **28 States** and **8 Union Territories**, covering approximately **6.1 lakh sample households** to provide comprehensive estimates for **707 districts**.
 
• **Gender Gap:** While the overall ratio is positive, the **Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB)** of **929** indicates that challenges regarding **son preference** and **gender-biased sex selection** still persist in society.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of an object increases with its _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **motion**. It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity.
 
• The mathematical expression for **kinetic energy** is **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** is the **mass** of the object and **v** is its **speed** or **velocity**.
 
• According to this formula, the **kinetic energy** of an object is **directly proportional** to the **square of its speed**. Therefore, if the **speed** of an object increases, its **kinetic energy** increases significantly. ***Hence, the statement that kinetic energy increases with speed is correct.***
 
• If the **speed** of an object is **doubled**, its **kinetic energy** becomes **four times** its original value because the speed is squared (2² = 4).
 
• For an object to have **kinetic energy**, it must be in **motion**; if the **speed** is **zero**, the **kinetic energy** will also be **zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass and Kinetic Energy**:

 
 
• **Kinetic energy** is also **directly proportional** to the **mass** of the object. If two objects move at the same **speed**, the object with the **greater mass** will possess more **kinetic energy**.
 
• For example, a **truck** moving at **50 km/h** has much more **kinetic energy** than a **bicycle** moving at the same **speed** due to the difference in their **mass**.
 
 
 
• **Friction**:
 
 
• **Friction** is a **force** that opposes **motion** between two surfaces. Instead of increasing **kinetic energy**, **friction** typically acts to **decrease** it by converting the energy into **thermal energy** (heat) or **sound energy**.
 
 
 
• **Volume and Density**:
 
 
• **Density** is the **mass per unit volume** of a substance. While **density** and **volume** determine the **mass** (Mass = Density x Volume), they do not directly dictate the increase in **kinetic energy** unless they result in a change in **mass** for an object already in **motion**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Units of Energy**: The **SI unit** of **kinetic energy** is the **Joule (J)**. **One Joule** is equal to **1 kg.m²/s²**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. If **positive work** is done, the **speed** increases; if **negative work** is done (like by friction), the **speed** decreases.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: **Kinetic energy** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**. This is why even if an object changes its **direction** of motion but maintains the same **speed**, its **kinetic energy** remains constant.
 
• **Potential Energy Comparison**: Unlike **kinetic energy**, **potential energy** is the energy stored in an object due to its **position** or **configuration** (e.g., height above the ground). The sum of **kinetic** and **potential energy** is known as **mechanical energy**.

questions.question: In March 2025, which country's government was accused of using a 'sonic weapon' against protestors, a device that emits painful sound waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Serbia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the government of **Serbia** was widely accused by international observers and human rights organizations of utilizing **sonic weapons** to suppress anti-government demonstrations in **Belgrade**.
 
• The specific device identified in these reports is the **Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD)**, a high-intensity hailing system that can emit directed beams of sound reaching painful decibel levels.
 
• The use of this technology occurred during a period of significant political tension in the **Balkan** nation, where **protesters** had gathered to voice concerns over electoral integrity and legislative changes.
 
• Medical reports from the scene indicated that individuals exposed to the device suffered from **acute hearing impairment**, **extreme vertigo**, and **nausea**, leading to a surge in hospitalizations among the civilian population.
 
• While the **Serbian** Ministry of Interior initially described the equipment as a "communication tool," the intensity of the sound waves used suggested a **deterrent** or weaponized application intended to forcibly clear public spaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD)**:

 
 
• Developed by **Genasys** (formerly **LRAD Corporation**), this device is a "non-lethal" weapon that sends messages or **deterrent tones** over much longer distances than normal loudspeakers.
 
• It was originally designed for **maritime security** following the **2000** attack on the **USS Cole** to warn approaching small boats.
 
 
 
• **Physical Impact and Decibel Levels**:
 
 
• The **LRAD 1000Xi** model can produce a maximum continuous output of **150 decibels (dB)**.
 
• Since the human **threshold of pain** is approximately **120 to 130 dB**, exposure to these levels can cause **permanent hearing loss** or **tinnitus** (ringing in the ears).
 
• The sound waves act on the **vestibular system** of the inner ear, which controls balance, often causing targets to fall or become physically incapacitated.
 
 
 
• **International Human Rights Context**:
 
 
• Organizations such as **Amnesty International** and **Human Rights Watch** have called for the regulation of acoustic devices, arguing they are **indiscriminate** and can affect peaceful bystanders and residents in nearby buildings.
 
• The use of these devices in **Europe** is subject to strict scrutiny under the **European Convention on Human Rights**, particularly regarding the **prohibition of torture** and degrading treatment.
 
 
 
• **Global Precedents**:
 
 
• Similar devices have been used for **crowd control** in the **United States** during the G20 summits and in **Australia** during pandemic-related protests, but the **2025** incident in **Serbia** is noted for the reported duration and intensity of the acoustic strikes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Functionality**: Unlike standard speakers that disperse sound in all directions, a **sonic weapon** uses **piezoelectric transducers** to create a narrow, "flashlight-like" beam of sound, allowing police to target specific groups without affecting officers standing behind the device.
 
• **Legal Classification**: In many jurisdictions, the **LRAD** is legally classified as a "communication device" rather than a **weapon**, which often allows police departments to bypass the stringent oversight required for **firearms** or **chemical agents** like tear gas.
 
• **March 2025 Timeline**: The escalation in **Serbia** reached its peak in mid-**March**, leading to a formal inquiry by the **European Parliament** regarding the export of such technologies to **non-EU** countries with histories of civil rights concerns.

questions.question: Which of the following port is located 105 Km downstream from Kolkata and has been constructed to reduce the congestion at Kolkata port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haldia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Haldia Port** was specifically constructed to function as a satellite port to the **Kolkata Port** to reduce the heavy congestion and pressure on the latter.
 
• It is situated at the confluence of the **Hooghly River** and the **Haldi River**, approximately **105 kilometers** downstream from the city of **Kolkata** in **West Bengal**.
 
• The port is better equipped to handle deep-draft vessels and bulk cargo like **petroleum**, **chemicals**, and **iron ore**, which are difficult for the riverine **Kolkata Port** to manage due to **siltation** issues.
 
• It is officially known as the **Haldia Dock Complex (HDC)** and functions under the administrative control of the **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port Trust** (formerly **Kolkata Port Trust**).
 
• The port serves a massive hinterland that includes the states of **West Bengal**, **Bihar**, **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**, and the landlocked neighboring countries of **Nepal** and **Bhutan**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Haldia**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kolkata Port:**

 
 
• It is the **only major riverine port** in **India**, located on the banks of the **Hooghly River**.
 
• Because it is a riverine port, it requires constant **dredging** to maintain the necessary depth for ships to navigate, especially due to the high **siltation** from the **Ganges** system.
 
 
 
• **Paradip Port:**
 
 
• Located in the **Jagatsinghpur** district of **Odisha**, it is a **deep-water, all-weather port** situated at the confluence of the **Mahanadi River** and the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It was the first major port on the **East Coast** commissioned after **Independence** in **1966** and is a premier gateway for exporting **iron ore** to **Japan** and other Southeast Asian nations.
 
 
 
• **Kandla Port:**
 
 
• Located in the **Gulf of Kutch** in **Gujarat**, it is now known as the **Deendayal Port**.
 
• It was developed in the **1950s** to serve as a substitute for the **Karachi Port**, which went to **Pakistan** after the **Partition** of **India** in **1947**. It is a **tidal port** and handles a large volume of crude oil and petroleum imports.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT):**
 
 
• Also known as **Nhava Sheva**, it is located in **Navi Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• Commissioned on **26 May 1989**, it is the largest **container port** in **India** and was built to decongest the **Mumbai Port**. It handles more than half of the total container traffic of all major ports in the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Major Ports in India:** India has **13 major ports** (12 government-controlled and 1 corporate) that handle about **95%** of India's foreign trade by volume and **70%** by value.
 
• **Geographical Distribution:** Ports like **Kandla**, **Mumbai**, **JNPT**, **Mormugao**, **New Mangalore**, and **Kochi** are located on the **West Coast**. Ports like **Tuticorin**, **Chennai**, **Ennore**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Paradip**, and **Kolkata/Haldia** are on the **East Coast**.
 
• **Sagarmala Programme:** Launched by the **Government of India** in **2015**, this initiative aims to promote **port-led development** and modernize India's coastline to reduce logistics costs for domestic and EXIM cargo.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Tat Vadya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dilruba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tat Vadya** is a category of musical instruments where sound is produced by the vibration of **strings**. These are also known as **Chordophones**.
 
• **Dilruba** is a traditional **stringed instrument** found mainly in **North India** and **Punjab**. It is played with a **bow** and has a neck similar to a **Sitar** and a soundbox similar to a **Sarangi**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Dilruba.***
 
• The **Dilruba** holds great significance in **Sikh history**, as it is believed to have been designed by the **10th Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh**, to make it easier for the Sikh warriors to carry the instrument on horseback compared to the heavier **Taus**.
 
• It features **metal strings** and **frets**, and the soundbox is covered with **goatskin** (parchment), which gives it a distinct, resonant tone often used in **Gurbani Sangeet** and **Indian Classical Music**.
 
• **Flute** is a wind instrument where sound is produced by a column of air. In Indian music classification, it is categorized as a **Sushira Vadya**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Dandia** are wooden sticks used primarily in the folk dance of **Gujarat**. Since they produce sound by being struck together, they are classified as **Ghan Vadya** (Idiophones). ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Musical Instruments (Natya Shastra):**

 
 
• The ancient treatise **Natya Shastra**, written by **Bharat Muni** (dated between **200 BCE and 200 CE**), classifies Indian musical instruments into **four** main categories based on how they produce sound.
 
• **Tat Vadya (Chordophones):** These are **stringed instruments**. The sound is produced by plucking, bowing, or striking the strings. Examples include **Sitar**, **Veena**, **Sarod**, **Santoor**, **Tanpura**, and **Ektara**.
 
• **Sushira Vadya (Aerophones):** These are **wind instruments** where sound is produced by air. Common examples are **Bansuri (Flute)**, **Shehnai**, **Pungi**, and **Harmonium**.
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya (Membranophones):** These are **percussion instruments** with a stretched skin or membrane that is struck to produce sound. Examples include **Tabla**, **Mridangam**, **Dholak**, and **Para** (a traditional drum).
 
• **Ghan Vadya (Idiophones):** These are **solid instruments** made of metal or wood that do not require a membrane. Sound is produced by striking two objects together. Examples include **Manjira (Cymbals)**, **Jaltarang**, **Ghatam**, and **Dandia**.
 
 
 
• **Detailed Features of Dilruba:**
 
 
• **Origin:** Developed in the **18th century** in the **Punjab region** of India.
 
• **Structure:** It consists of approximately **18 to 22 sympathetic strings** and **4 main strings**. The frets are movable, allowing the player to adjust for different **Ragas**.
 
• **Use:** It is widely used in **shabad kirtan** and was historically popular in **Santour** and **Rabindra Sangeet**.
 
 
 
• **Para and Dandia:**
 
 
• **Para (or Parai):** One of the oldest **drums** used in **Tamil Nadu**, specifically in folk music. It is an **Avanaddha Vadya**.
 
• **Dandia:** These are typically made of **bamboo** or **teak wood** and are synonymous with the **Navratri festival** in **Western India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Santoor** is a unique **Tat Vadya** because, unlike the Sitar which is plucked, the strings of the Santoor are struck with lightweight **wooden mallets** or hammers.
 
• The **Veena** is often considered the mother of all stringed instruments in **Carnatic music** and is associated with **Goddess Saraswati**.
 
• In **2015**, the **Dilruba** and **Taus** saw a revival in the **Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)** as the **Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC)** encouraged the use of traditional string instruments over the harmonium.

questions.question: Which country is ranked 1st in the Global Firepower Index 2025 with the lowest Power Index score of 0.0744?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United States of America (USA)** has been ranked **1st** in the **Global Firepower (GFP) Index 2025**, maintaining its position as the world's most powerful military.
 
• The **USA** achieved the lowest and most favorable **Power Index (PwrIndx)** score of **0.0744**. In this indexing system, a score of **0.0000** is considered the "perfect" score, meaning the lower the numerical value, the higher the nation's theoretical fighting capability.
 
• The **2025 Global Firepower ranking** utilized more than **60 individual factors** to determine a given nation's **Power Index** score, ranging from military might and financials to logistical capability and geography.
 
• The assessment included a total of **145 world powers**, providing a comprehensive look at the conventional war-making capabilities of nations across the globe.
 
• The **USA** remains at the top due to its massive **defense budget**, advanced **technological integration**, and significant lead in **airpower** and **naval carrier** fleets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Top Ranked Nations in 2025**:

 
 
• **Russia**: Ranked **2nd** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.0768**.
 
• **China**: Ranked **3rd** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.0772**, closely trailing Russia.
 
• **India**: Ranked **4th** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.1087**, solidifying its status as a major regional and global military power.
 
• **South Korea**: Ranked **5th**, showing significant growth in military manufacturing and exports.
 
 
 
• **Methodology of the Index**:
 
 
• The **Global Firepower Index** has been compiled since **2006**. It focuses strictly on **conventional capabilities** and does not take **nuclear stockpiles** into account for the direct score, though it considers them as a general strategic deterrent.
 
• Factors weighed include **manpower** (available population and active personnel), **equipment** (tanks, aircraft, naval units), **natural resources** (oil production/reserves), and **financial stability**.
 
• The ranking allows smaller, but more technologically advanced, nations to compete with larger, less-developed ones by applying specific **modifiers** (penalties and bonuses) to the raw data.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographic and Economic Factors**: The index rewards nations with high **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** and strong **logistical infrastructure**, such as **ports**, **terminals**, and **roadway networks**, as these are vital for sustaining long-term military operations.
 
• **Budgetary Dominance**: The **USA** defense budget remains the largest in the world, often exceeding **$800 billion**, which is greater than the next several countries combined. This enables the **United States** to maintain **11 nuclear-powered aircraft carriers**, a feat unmatched by any other nation.
 
• **Regional Trends**: In the **2025** report, there is a notable trend of **Asian nations** (specifically **China, India, and South Korea**) increasing their dominance in the top 5, reflecting a shift in global military investment toward the **Indo-Pacific** region.
